content: One year following the publication of the guidelines, an evaluation will be conducted to assess their immediate impact. This evaluation will take the form of an online survey targeting various stakeholders, such as professional societies and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). The purpose of this survey is to determine the extent to which the guidelines have been utilized within countries, whether any of the recommendations have been implemented, and how they may have influenced policy decisions. Additionally, this short-term impact evaluation will include an analysis of barriers to effective implementation. This feedback will be critical for the development of derivative products and for making future modifications to the guidelines. During the development of the guidelines, the Evidence and Recommendation Review Groups (ERRGs) and the Guideline Development Group (GDG) identified several gaps in evidence and areas requiring further research. These include: The safety and efficacy of surgical abortion procedures at gestational ages of 12 weeks or more, as well as the use of vacuum aspiration for incomplete abortion. The feasibility of pharmacists administering injectable contraceptives in lowand middle-resource settings, which would require implementation research. The impact of social marketing and social franchising approaches on abortion care, as assessed through evaluation research. Determining the most appropriate prescribing and dispensing authorities for abortion medications, including comparisons between self-sourced abortion medicines and those prescribed or dispensed by trained healthcare workers. Mechanisms to ensure that individuals managing medical abortion on their own have access to pain management medications and contraceptive methods. The acceptability and satisfaction levels associated with various service delivery approaches for providing quality abortion care to transgender, nonbinary, and intersex individuals. In the context of universal health coverage (UHC), health financing, and access to essential commodities, further research is needed to evaluate the impact of changes to the WHO Model Lists of Essential Medicines, particularly regarding the mifepristone and misoprostol combination regimen. For monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of abortion care, the following areas require attention: The development and validation of indicators that incorporate social and economic disability, in addition to physical disability, when calculating years lived with abortion-related disability. This aligns with the growing focus on global burden of disease and disability estimation. The creation and validation of standardized data-verification methods to ensure abortion-related data can be presented with a verification score. This effort aims to address the underreporting of abortion-related data due to stigma. The development and increased use of qualitative methods for M&E of quality abortion care, which would help identify barriers to progress and enablers for strengthening health system performance.
